blockers.title: Registration happens inside each customer's tenant
blockers.detail: Per integration docs, each customer's Workday administrator registers an API client in their own tenant and gives you a separate client id and secret.
blockers.workaround: Send the customer's administrator the request message below.

blockers.title: Two permission layers
blockers.detail: Functional-area scopes on the API client and domain security policies for the authorizing account's security group are separate. A correct scope is not enough.
blockers.workaround: Ask the administrator to add the needed domain security policies and activate pending changes.

blockers.title: OAuth 2.0 must be enabled in the tenant
blockers.detail: The tenant's security setup must have OAuth 2.0 enabled before an API client can be registered.
blockers.workaround: Ask the administrator to enable it under Edit Tenant Setup - Security.

steps.title: Involve the customer's Workday administrator
steps.action: Ask a Workday administrator for the customer's tenant to do the registration steps below. Send them the request message from this guide.

steps.title: Enable OAuth 2.0 in the tenant
steps.action: In Workday, search for Edit Tenant Setup - Security and make sure OAuth 2.0 is enabled.

steps.title: Register an API client
steps.action: Run Register API Client (authorization code grant) for user-based access, or Register API Client for Integrations for integration system user flows. Save the client id and secret; the secret is shown once.

fields.name: Client Grant Type
fields.guidance: Authorization Code Grant for user-based OAuth

fields.name: Scope (Functional Areas)
fields.guidance: Only the functional areas you need, such as System, Human Resources or Staffing

fields.name: Non-Expiring Refresh Tokens
fields.guidance: Enable it if you will store a refresh token; integration docs say refresh tokens must not expire

steps.title: Grant security policies
steps.action: If you use an integration system user, create the user and a security group, add the domain security policies your scopes need, and activate pending security policy changes.

steps.title: Collect endpoints and test authorization
steps.action: Get the tenant-specific authorize, token and REST hosts from the administrator, then test the authorization code flow.

evidence.claim: OAuth 2.0 must be enabled in tenant security setup; scopes are functional areas and the account also needs matching domain security policies.
Each customer's administrator registers an API client in their own tenant and hands over a separate client id and secret; there are two permission layers; hosts are tenant-specific.
